Northgate Digital Services is an independent technology consultancy based in Manchester. We help housing associations and local councils improve the way they run their services, and we are proud of our open, supportive culture. Our people are our greatest asset.

About the role
We are recruiting a Senior Business Analyst to join a delivery team working on a tenant portal for a large housing provider. You will act as the link between residents, operational teams and developers, turning needs into clear and testable requirements.

Responsibilities
- Run workshops with stakeholders to capture processes and pain points
- Write user stories with clear acceptance criteria and maintain the backlog
- Produce process maps, wireframes and data flow diagrams
- Support user acceptance testing and help the team resolve defects
- Present options and recommendations to senior stakeholders
- Mentor junior analysts and share good practice across the practice

Requirements
- 5+ years' experience as a business analyst, ideally on digital service projects
- Strong knowledge of agile delivery and tools such as Jira and Confluence
- Excellent written and spoken communication
- A degree or equivalent practical experience
- Experience in the social housing sector would be an advantage

Benefits
We offer a salary of £55,000 to £62,000, 28 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, a pension with 6% employer contribution, private medical cover, a cycle-to-work scheme and a generous training budget. Our office is five minutes from Piccadilly station, and we work in a hybrid pattern with two days a week together. We were founded 12 years ago and have kept our team small enough to know everyone by name.

We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from everyone. Adjustments are available at every stage of our recruitment process. To apply, please send your CV and a short covering note describing a project you are proud of. Interviews will be held over two stages in the coming weeks.

text:
Our client is a well-known regional building society with a strong reputation for customer service. They are investing heavily in digital change and are now looking for a Project Manager to lead a portfolio of customer-facing initiatives.

The role
Reporting to the Head of Change, you will take ownership of projects from initiation through to benefits realisation. You will work with colleagues across lending, operations, risk and technology, and you will be the main point of accountability for time, cost and quality.

Key responsibilities:
* Plan and manage projects of up to £3m, using both waterfall and agile approaches
* Maintain RAID logs, financial forecasts and clear status reporting
* Manage third-party suppliers and agree statements of work
* Chair steering groups and escalate issues in good time
* Coach team members and build effective working relationships

About you
You will have 3-5 years of project management experience in financial services or another regulated sector. You are a confident communicator who can influence at all levels. A recognised qualification such as PRINCE2 or APM is desirable. You are comfortable working with MS Project and can pick up new tools quickly.

What is on offer
A salary of up to £68,000 depending on experience, an annual bonus of up to 10%, 30 days holiday, a defined contribution pension and a flexible approach to working from home. The society offers an enhanced long service award after 10 years, and a structured development path with support towards professional qualifications. The contract is permanent and the location is Leeds city centre, with some travel to other offices in the north of England.

Please note that all offers are subject to satisfactory references and a credit check. We encourage early applications because we expect strong interest, and we review CVs as they arrive.
note: range in About you; long service award is a trap

Brightwater Learning is a charity that supports adults returning to education across the Midlands. We run community courses, an online learning platform and a careers advice service, and we are growing quickly.

The opportunity
We are looking for a Data Analyst to help us understand who we reach and what difference we make. This is a new post in a small data team, and you will have real influence over how we measure impact.

What you will do
- Build and maintain dashboards in Power BI for trustees and funders
- Clean, combine and analyse data from our learning platform and CRM
- Prepare quarterly impact reports and answer ad hoc questions from colleagues
- Help colleagues use data well, through short training sessions
- Make sure data is handled in line with GDPR and our retention schedule

What we are looking for
You are curious, careful and good at explaining numbers in plain English. You are confident with SQL and Excel, and you have used a visualisation tool before. We care more about how you think than about job titles, so if you have gained your skills through study, volunteering or a career change, please apply. Experience in the charity or education sector is welcome, though not needed.

What we offer
- Salary £34,000 to £38,000, depending on experience
- 27 days annual leave plus bank holidays, rising with length of service
- Employer pension contribution of 8%
- Hybrid working from our Birmingham office
- Paid volunteering days and a wellbeing allowance
- Personal development budget and regular one-to-ones with your manager

We are committed to being an inclusive employer. We guarantee an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria. Closing date is Friday 20 November, with interviews the following week. Please apply with your CV and a short statement of up to 400 words about why this work matters to you.

Harlow & Finch Logistics has been moving goods around the UK since 1994. With a fleet of over 300 vehicles and four distribution centres, we deliver for supermarkets, manufacturers and online retailers. This year we began a five-year programme to digitise our warehouses, and we need talented people to help us do it.

Role summary
As IT Service Desk Analyst you will be the first point of contact for colleagues who need help with laptops, handheld scanners, printers and business applications. This is a busy, practical role at our Daventry head office, with the chance to grow into second-line support.

Duties
- Log, prioritise and resolve incidents and requests using our ITSM system
- Set up new starters and manage accounts in Microsoft 365 and Active Directory
- Support warehouse staff on shift, including some evening work
- Keep knowledge articles up to date and spot recurring problems
- Escalate complex issues to the infrastructure team with clear notes

Person specification
- Good working knowledge of Windows 11 and Microsoft 365
- A calm, friendly manner with non-technical users
- Willingness to work a rota covering 7am to 7pm
- A full UK driving licence, as occasional travel between sites is needed
- Relevant qualifications such as ITIL Foundation or CompTIA A+ are helpful

Benefits
You will receive £28,500 per year, overtime at enhanced rates, a contributory pension, free parking, a staff canteen and discounts with local retailers. Employees receive a long service award after 5 years, and we promote from within wherever possible: three of our current team leaders started on the service desk. Our graduate and apprenticeship schemes run for 3 years and give a route into infrastructure and project work.

If you would like to join us, please apply online with your CV. We will contact shortlisted candidates within a week and hold interviews at Daventry. All appointments are subject to a satisfactory background check.

Aldermoor Analytics is a data consultancy working with energy and utilities clients. Our team of 60 builds data platforms, models and reporting that help our clients make decisions with confidence. We are based in Edinburgh and work with colleagues across the UK.

Senior Data Engineer
We are expanding our engineering practice and are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to design and build cloud data pipelines. You will lead technical work on client projects, and you will help us set standards for the team.

You will
- Design robust ELT pipelines on Azure using Data Factory, Databricks and Synapse
- Model data warehouses and data lakes to support analytics and machine learning
- Review code, write tests and automate deployments through CI/CD
- Talk with clients to understand their needs and explain technical choices
- Mentor engineers and take part in our hiring

You have
- 7+ years of experience in data engineering or a closely related field
- Expert SQL and Python
- Experience designing and running pipelines in a cloud environment
- A habit of writing clear documentation
- Good judgement about when to keep things simple

Nice to have: Terraform, Spark Structured Streaming, and experience with time-series data from sensors.

Our package
Salary of £70,000 to £85,000, a discretionary bonus, 30 days of leave, a pension at 7% employer contribution, a laptop of your choice and a conference budget. We offer flexible hours, and you can work from home most of the week, with a trip to Edinburgh once a fortnight for team days. We keep project data for 6 years after contract end, so you will take part in a documented handover process on every engagement.

To apply, send your CV and a link to any code or write-ups you would like us to see. We aim to respond to every application within five working days. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the process.
note: requirement among 'You have'; retention is a trap

Welcome to Kestrel Community Housing, a not-for-profit landlord looking after 9,000 homes in Kent. We believe good housing changes lives, and our staff work every day to make that real for our residents.

About the post
We are looking for a Digital Project Support Officer to help our small change team deliver a range of projects, from new repairs booking tools to improvements to our website. You will keep plans organised, track tasks and make sure people know what is happening.

Main tasks
- Maintain project plans, risk logs and action trackers
- Arrange meetings, take notes and follow up actions
- Gather feedback from residents and colleagues
- Help test new features and report issues to suppliers
- Prepare simple reports for the change board
- Assist with training sessions for staff

About you
We want someone organised, who enjoys working with people and has the confidence to chase things up politely. You will have worked in an office or project environment and have a good level of Microsoft Excel. Some knowledge of agile methods would be useful. A project qualification is welcome but not necessary, and we will support you to study for one.

Package
Salary of £29,000 to £32,000, 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, a pension scheme, an employee assistance programme and a free eye test. Our offices are in Maidstone, and we are happy to talk about flexible and part-time arrangements. This is a permanent post, and there is a clear route to Project Coordinator within a short period of time as you build experience.

Kestrel is a Disability Confident employer. If you need the advert in another format, please call our recruitment team. Applications close at midday on Monday 23 November.

Redline Software is a product company building scheduling software used by NHS trusts and private clinics. Our platform has been trusted by clinicians for more than 15 years, and we release new features every fortnight. We are a team of 85 split across Bristol and remote working.

The role: Full Stack Developer
You will join one of our four product squads and work on features from idea to release. You will write code on both the front end and the back end, and you will help us keep a high standard of quality and security.

Responsibilities
- Build and maintain features using React, TypeScript and Node.js
- Design and expose APIs and work with a PostgreSQL database
- Write unit and integration tests and take part in code reviews
- Support live services and take part in a fair on-call rota
- Work with designers and product managers to refine ideas

Skills and experience
Candidates should have a minimum of 2 years' commercial experience building web applications with a modern JavaScript framework. You will understand REST principles, version control with Git and automated testing. Knowledge of healthcare standards such as HL7 or FHIR would be a bonus. We welcome people from non-traditional backgrounds, including bootcamp graduates.

Benefits
- £42,000 to £52,000 depending on experience
- 25 days holiday, plus your birthday off
- Enhanced parental leave
- Learning budget of £1,200 per year
- Share options after a 1 year probation period
- Home working allowance and a monthly team lunch

Our hiring process has three steps: a short call, a practical task you can do in your own time, and a final conversation with the squad you would join. We aim to complete the whole process within two weeks and give feedback to everyone.
note: requirement under Skills; company age, learning budget, probation are traps

Our client is a leading UK insurer undertaking one of the largest change programmes in its history, and it is seeking a Head of Programme Delivery to take charge of a portfolio worth over £50m. This is a high-profile role with direct access to the executive team.

Overview
You will lead a team of programme and project managers delivering technology and operational change across claims, underwriting and customer service. You will own the delivery plan, the budget and the relationship with the board. The programme is planned over 4 years, with the first major release due next summer.

Responsibilities
- Set the delivery approach and governance for the programme
- Report progress, risks and benefits to the executive committee
- Manage budgets, forecasts and supplier contracts
- Build and develop a high-performing team of eight direct reports
- Work with the regulator and internal audit where required
- Create a culture of accountability and open challenge

Essential experience
- A minimum of 10 years' experience in programme or portfolio management within financial services
- A record of delivering multi-million-pound change on time and within budget
- Strong commercial awareness and supplier management skills
- Senior stakeholder management and excellent presentation skills
- MSP, PMP or equivalent qualification

Package and location
The base salary is up to £120,000, with a bonus of up to 20% and a car allowance. You will receive a pension, private medical insurance for you and your family, and 28 days of holiday. The role is based in London with two days a week working from home. The company offers a long service award after 10 years and has been named a top employer for 7 consecutive years.

Interested candidates should send their CV in confidence. All discussions will be treated as strictly private, and we will not share your details without your permission. We expect to hold first interviews in early December.
note: Essential experience bullet; programme length and awards are traps

text:
Millbrook Technical Services supplies engineering and IT support to schools across Yorkshire. For 18 years we have kept classrooms connected, and our friendly team is trusted by more than 120 schools.

We are recruiting a Network Engineer to join our field team. You will travel between schools to install, configure and maintain networks, wireless systems and firewalls, and you will help school staff make the most of their technology.

What you will be doing
- Installing and maintaining switches, access points and firewalls
- Troubleshooting network faults and carrying out root cause analysis
- Managing VLANs, DHCP and DNS in Windows Server environments
- Documenting networks and keeping inventories up to date
- Completing planned maintenance during school holidays
- Advising on security and safeguarding filtering

What we are looking for
You will have 4-6 years of experience in a network engineering or infrastructure role. You will know Cisco, Ubiquiti or similar kit well. A CCNA or equivalent is expected. As you will work with children's data and be on school sites, you must be willing to undergo an enhanced DBS check. Experience in an education setting is a plus, though not essential.

Rewards
Salary of £38,000 to £44,000, a company van for work use, 25 days of leave and bank holidays, a pension, and a Christmas bonus. All staff receive a service award after 3 years, and a tools and equipment allowance of £500 per year. School holiday working patterns mean your time is varied, with a mix of site visits and remote work.

We interview on a rolling basis and may close the vacancy early. To apply, send your CV with a covering message that tells us about a network problem you solved and how you did it.
note: range in 'looking for'; company age, service award, allowance traps

text:
Tamar Health Partnership is a group of GP practices across Cornwall working together to deliver better care. We are seeking a Clinical Systems Lead to look after the digital tools our clinicians rely on each day.

About the job
You will be responsible for how clinical systems are set up, used and improved across 11 practices. This includes the electronic patient record, appointment systems and reporting tools. You will work with GPs, nurses and managers, and you will have a direct effect on patient care.

Key duties
- Configure templates, protocols and searches in the clinical system
- Train and support clinical and administrative staff
- Run data quality checks and prepare reports for commissioners
- Manage system access and information governance requirements
- Work with suppliers on upgrades and incident resolution
- Lead small improvement projects across practices

Requirements
Essential: strong knowledge of a GP clinical system such as SystmOne or EMIS, and a good understanding of data protection and patient confidentiality. You should be organised and able to explain technical ideas simply. Desirable: 3+ years of experience in a similar role in primary care, and a qualification in health informatics.

Terms
The post is full-time on a 2 year fixed-term contract, with the potential to become permanent. Salary is £40,000 to £46,000 on the NHS-style pay bands used by the partnership, with 27 days of leave plus bank holidays, rising to 33 days after 5 years of service. The NHS pension scheme is available. The main base is Truro, with travel between practices, so a driving licence and access to a car are essential.

For an informal chat, please contact the practice manager. Closing date: 30 November. We value diversity and encourage applications from all sections of the community.
note: years only as desirable; contract and leave are traps
